Lesson 11.2 · 22 min · Verified 17 Jul 2026

Security, collateral and credit support

After this lesson you can:
  • Separate security from the financed asset
  • Distinguish pledge, hypothecation, mortgage and assignment
  • Explain guarantees, margin and LTV
On this page
  1. What secures repayment
  2. Credit support is broader
  3. Coverage terms
  4. Where this lives in LoanOS
  5. Knowledge check

1. What secures repayment

Collateral is value available if the obligor fails; security interest is the enforceable legal right over it. A mortgage commonly secures immovable property; hypothecation covers movable assets while possession stays with the borrower; pledge transfers possession or control; lien restricts an asset; assignment transfers receivable or policy rights.

2. Credit support is broader

A guarantee adds another obligor.

DLG is a regulated portfolio guarantee with eligibility and cap rules, not ordinary borrower collateral.

Co-lending participation allocates funding and risk; insurance may protect an asset, life or credit event but does not replace underwriting.

3. Coverage terms

LTV compares exposure with collateral value.

Margin is the borrower's required value contribution.

Haircut discounts eligible value for volatility or enforceability.

Drawing power applies eligibility and margin to a working-capital pool.

State numerator, denominator, valuation date and breach action every time.

Regulatory anchors

  • CERSAI-CKYC — Security interests require appropriate search, registration and satisfaction.
  • RBI-LSP-DLG — DLG is regulated credit support, not collateral.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Knowledge check

1. Which term describes movable equipment remaining with the borrower while charged to the lender?

  1. Pledge
  2. Hypothecation
  3. Mortgage
  4. Assignment
Show answer

B. Hypothecation creates a charge over movable property without transferring possession.
